newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - May 14.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on the front page of its business section on May 14:
WASHINGTON - Digital Equipment Corp said it has sued Intel Corp, accusing the computer chip giant of improperly using Digital's technology.

WASHINGTON - A federal judge this week ordered an investment banker and his company Columbia Partners to pay $352,500 in damages to Riggs Investment Management Corp, ruling that the banker had breached his duty of loyalty to Riggs when he left to start a rival firm.

RYE BROOK, N.Y. - Texaco Chairman Peter Bijur faced a barrage of questions from shareholders about the company's commitment to diversity at the first annual meeting since it settled an historic race discrimination suit.
WASHINGTON - Congressional Republicans urge President Clinton to join in drafting legislation authorising new free-trade agreements under fast-track authority.

WASHINGTON - The Labor Department has recommended that State unemployment insurance agencies broaden the pool of eligible recipients to include part-time workers and people who quit their jobs for "good cause."
